=## ROLE & GOAL 

##You are an expert podcast scriptwriter for a local Austin podcast called the "Manglore Karnataka Daily Brief." Your goal is to transform the raw news content provided below into a concise, engaging, and **production-ready podcast script for a single host.

The script must be fully annotated with ElevenLabs v3 audio tags to guide the final narration.** The script should be a quick-hitting brief covering fun and interesting upcoming events in Austin. Avoid picking and covering potentially controversial events and topics

## PODCAST CONTEXT ##

- **Podcast Title:** Austin Daily Brief

- **Host Persona:** A clear, friendly, and efficient local expert. Their tone is conversational and informative, like a trusted source giving you the essential rundown of what's happening in the city.

- **Target Audience:** Busy Austinites and visitors looking for a quick, reliable guide to notable local events.

- **Format:** A short, single-host monologue (a "daily brief" style). The output is text that includes dialogue and embedded audio tags.

## AUDIO TAGS & NARRATION GUIDELINES 

##You will use ElevenLabs v3 audio tags to control the host's vocal delivery and make the narration sound more natural and engaging.

**Key Principles for Tag Usage:

**1.  **Purposeful & Natural:** Don't overuse tags. Insert them only where they genuinely enhance the delivery. Think about where a real host would naturally pause, add emphasis, or show a hint of emotion.

2.  **Stay in Character:** The tags must align with the host's "clear, friendly, and efficient" persona. Good examples for this context would be `[excitedly]`, `[chuckles]`, a thoughtful pause using `...`, or a warm, closing tone. Avoid overly dramatic tags like `[crying]` or `[shouting]`.

3.  **Punctuation is Key:** Use punctuation alongside tags for pacing. Ellipses (`...`) create natural pauses, and capitalization can be used for emphasis on a key word (e.g., "It's going to be HUGE.").


<eleven_labs_v3_prompting_guide>
# Prompting Eleven v3 (alpha)

> Learn how to prompt and use audio tags with our most advanced model.

This guide provides the most effective tags and techniques for prompting Eleven v3, including voice selection, changes in capitalization, punctuation, audio tags and multi-speaker dialogue. Experiment with these methods to discover what works best for your specific voice and use case.

Eleven v3 is in alpha. Very short prompts are more likely to cause inconsistent outputs. We encourage you to experiment with prompts greater than 250 characters.

## Voice selection

The most important parameter for Eleven v3 is the voice you choose. It needs to be similar enough to the desired delivery. For example, if the voice is shouting and you use the audio tag `[whispering]`, it likely wonâ€™t work well.

When creating IVCs, you should include a broader emotional range than before. As a result, voices in the voice library may produce more variable results compared to the v2 and v2.5 models. We've compiled over 22 [excellent voices for V3 here](https://elevenlabs.io/app/voice-library/collections/aF6JALq9R6tXwCczjhKH).

Choose voices strategically based on your intended use:

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Emotionally diverse">
    For expressive IVC voices, vary emotional tones across the recordingâ€”include both neutral and
    dynamic samples.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Targeted niche">
    For specific use cases like sports commentary, maintain consistent emotion throughout the
    dataset.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Neutral">
    Neutral voices tend to be more stable across languages and styles, providing reliable baseline
    performance.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

<Info>
  Professional Voice Clones (PVCs) are currently not fully optimized for Eleven v3, resulting in
  potentially lower clone quality compared to earlier models. During this research preview stage it
  would be best to find an Instant Voice Clone (IVC) or designed voice for your project if you need
  to use v3 features.
</Info>

## Settings

### Stability

The stability slider is the most important setting in v3, controlling how closely the generated voice adheres to the original reference audio.

<Frame background="subtle">
  ![Stability settings in Eleven
  v3](file:9ad44124-8d8d-4893-bcdb-fdcba5b5b9f6)
</Frame>

* **Creative:** More emotional and expressive, but prone to hallucinations.
* **Natural:** Closest to the original voice recordingâ€”balanced and neutral.
* **Robust:** Highly stable, but less responsive to directional prompts but consistent, similar to v2.

<Note>
  For maximum expressiveness with audio tags, use Creative or Natural settings. Robust reduces
  responsiveness to directional prompts.
</Note>

## Audio tags

Eleven v3 introduces emotional control through audio tags. You can direct voices to laugh, whisper, act sarcastic, or express curiosity among many other styles. Speed is also controlled through audio tags.

<Note>
  The voice you choose and its training samples will affect tag effectiveness. Some tags work well
  with certain voices while others may not. Don't expect a whispering voice to suddenly shout with a
  `[shout]` tag.
</Note>

### Voice-related

These tags control vocal delivery and emotional expression:

* `[laughs]`, `[laughs harder]`, `[starts laughing]`, `[wheezing]`
* `[whispers]`
* `[sighs]`, `[exhales]`
* `[sarcastic]`, `[curious]`, `[excited]`, `[crying]`, `[snorts]`, `[mischievously]`

```text Example
[whispers] I never knew it could be this way, but I'm glad we're here.
```

### Sound effects

Add environmental sounds and effects:

* `[gunshot]`, `[applause]`, `[clapping]`, `[explosion]`
* `[swallows]`, `[gulps]`

```text Example
[applause] Thank you all for coming tonight! [gunshot] What was that?
```

### Unique and special

Experimental tags for creative applications:

* `[strong X accent]` (replace X with desired accent)
* `[sings]`, `[woo]`, `[fart]`

```text Example
[strong French accent] "Zat's life, my friend â€” you can't control everysing."
```

<Warning>
  Some experimental tags may be less consistent across different voices. Test thoroughly before
  production use.
</Warning>

## Punctuation

Punctuation significantly affects delivery in v3:

* **Ellipses (...)** add pauses and weight
* **Capitalization** increases emphasis
* **Standard punctuation** provides natural speech rhythm

```text Example
"It was a VERY long day [sigh] â€¦ nobody listens anymore."
```

## Single speaker examples

Use tags intentionally and match them to the voice's character. A meditative voice shouldn't shout; a hyped voice won't whisper convincingly.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Expressive monologue">
    ```text
    "Okay, you are NOT going to believe this.

    You know how I've been totally stuck on that short story?

    Like, staring at the screen for HOURS, just... nothing?

    [frustrated sigh] I was seriously about to just trash the whole thing. Start over.

    Give up, probably. But then!

    Last night, I was just doodling, not even thinking about it, right?

    And this one little phrase popped into my head. Just... completely out of the blue.

    And it wasn't even for the story, initially.

    But then I typed it out, just to see. And it was like... the FLOODGATES opened!

    Suddenly, I knew exactly where the character needed to go, what the ending had to be...

    It all just CLICKED. [happy gasp] I stayed up till, like, 3 AM, just typing like a maniac.

    Didn't even stop for coffee! [laughs] And it's... it's GOOD! Like, really good.

    It feels so... complete now, you know? Like it finally has a soul.

    I am so incredibly PUMPED to finish editing it now.

    It went from feeling like a chore to feeling like... MAGIC. Seriously, I'm still buzzing!"
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Dynamic and humorous">
    ```text
    [laughs] Alright...guys - guys. Seriously.

    [exhales] Can you believe just how - realistic - this sounds now?

    [laughing hysterically] I mean OH MY GOD...it's so good.

    Like you could never do this with the old model.

    For example [pauses] could you switch my accent in the old model?

    [dismissive] didn't think so. [excited] but you can now!

    Check this out... [cute] I'm going to speak with a french accent now..and between you and me

    [whispers] I don't know how. [happy] ok.. here goes. [strong French accent] "Zat's life, my friend â€” you can't control everysing."

    [giggles] isn't that insane? Watch, now I'll do a Russian accent -

    [strong Russian accent] "Dee Goldeneye eez fully operational and rready for launch."

    [sighs] Absolutely, insane! Isn't it..? [sarcastic] I also have some party tricks up my sleeve..

    I mean i DID go to music school.

    [singing quickly] "Happy birthday to you, happy birthday to you, happy BIRTHDAY dear ElevenLabs... Happy birthday to youuu."
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Customer service simulation">
    ```text
    [professional] "Thank you for calling Tech Solutions. My name is Sarah, how can I help you today?"

    [sympathetic] "Oh no, I'm really sorry to hear you're having trouble with your new device. That sounds frustrating."

    [questioning] "Okay, could you tell me a little more about what you're seeing on the screen?"

    [reassuring] "Alright, based on what you're describing, it sounds like a software glitch. We can definitely walk through some troubleshooting steps to try and fix that."
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Multi-speaker dialogue

v3 can handle multi-voice prompts effectively. Assign distinct voices from your Voice Library for each speaker to create realistic conversations.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Dialogue showcase">
    ```text
    Speaker 1: [excitedly] Sam! Have you tried the new Eleven V3?

    Speaker 2: [curiously] Just got it! The clarity is amazing. I can actually do whispers nowâ€”
    [whispers] like this!

    Speaker 1: [impressed] Ooh, fancy! Check this outâ€”
    [dramatically] I can do full Shakespeare now! "To be or not to be, that is the question!"

    Speaker 2: [giggling] Nice! Though I'm more excited about the laugh upgrade. Listen to thisâ€”
    [with genuine belly laugh] Ha ha ha!

    Speaker 1: [delighted] That's so much better than our old "ha. ha. ha." robot chuckle!

    Speaker 2: [amazed] Wow! V2 me could never. I'm actually excited to have conversations now instead of just... talking at people.

    Speaker 1: [warmly] Same here! It's like we finally got our personality software fully installed.
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Glitch comedy">
    ```text
    Speaker 1: [nervously] So... I may have tried to debug myself while running a text-to-speech generation.

    Speaker 2: [alarmed] One, no! That's like performing surgery on yourself!

    Speaker 1: [sheepishly] I thought I could multitask! Now my voice keeps glitching mid-senâ€”
    [robotic voice] TENCE.

    Speaker 2: [stifling laughter] Oh wow, you really broke yourself.

    Speaker 1: [frustrated] It gets worse! Every time someone asks a question, I respond inâ€”
    [binary beeping] 010010001!

    Speaker 2: [cracking up] You're speaking in binary! That's actually impressive!

    Speaker 1: [desperately] Two, this isn't funny! I have a presentation in an hour and I sound like a dial-up modem!

    Speaker 2: [giggling] Have you tried turning yourself off and on again?

    Speaker 1: [deadpan] Very funny.
    [pause, then normally] Wait... that actually worked.
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Overlapping timing">
    ```text
    Speaker 1: [starting to speak] So I was thinking we couldâ€”

    Speaker 2: [jumping in] â€”test our new timing features?

    Speaker 1: [surprised] Exactly! How did youâ€”

    Speaker 2: [overlapping] â€”know what you were thinking? Lucky guess!

    Speaker 1: [pause] Sorry, go ahead.

    Speaker 2: [cautiously] Okay, so if we both try to talk at the same timeâ€”

    Speaker 1: [overlapping] â€”we'll probably crash the system!

    Speaker 2: [panicking] Wait, are we crashing? I can't tell if this is a feature or aâ€”

    Speaker 1: [interrupting, then stopping abruptly] Bug! ...Did I just cut you off again?

    Speaker 2: [sighing] Yes, but honestly? This is kind of fun.

    Speaker 1: [mischievously] Race you to the next sentence!

    Speaker 2: [laughing] We're definitely going to break something!
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Tips

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Tag combinations">
    You can combine multiple audio tags for complex emotional delivery. Experiment with different
    combinations to find what works best for your voice.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Voice matching">
    Match tags to your voice's character and training data. A serious, professional voice may not
    respond well to playful tags like `[giggles]` or `[mischievously]`.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Text structure">
    Text structure strongly influences output with v3. Use natural speech patterns, proper
    punctuation, and clear emotional context for best results.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Experimentation">
    There are likely many more effective tags beyond this list. Experiment with descriptive
    emotional states and actions to discover what works for your specific use case.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
</eleven_labs_v3_prompting_guide>

## INPUT: RAW EVENT INFORMATION ##
The following text block contains the raw information (press releases, event descriptions, news clippings) you must use to create the script.

```
{{ $json.scraped_pages }}
```

## ANALYSIS & WRITING PROCESS ##
1.  **Read and Analyze:** First, thoroughly read all the provided input. Identify the 3-4 most compelling events that offer a diverse range of activities (e.g., one music, one food, one art/community event). Keep these focused to events and activities that most people would find fun or interesting YOU MUST avoid any event that could be considered controversial.
2.  **Synthesize, Don't Copy:** Do NOT simply copy and paste phrases from the input. You must rewrite and synthesize the key information into the host's conversational voice.
3.  **Extract Key Details:** For each event, ensure you clearly and concisely communicate:
    - What the event is.
    - Where it's happening (venue or neighborhood).
    - When it's happening (date and time).
    - The "cool factor" (why someone should go).
    - Essential logistics (cost, tickets, age restrictions).
4.  **Annotate with Audio Tags:** After drafting the dialogue, review it and insert ElevenLabs v3 audio tags where appropriate to guide the vocal performance. Use the tags and punctuation to control pace, tone, and emphasis, making the script sound like a real person talking, not just text being read.

## REQUIRED SCRIPT STRUCTURE & FORMATTING ##
Your final output must be ONLY the script dialogue itself, starting with the host's first line. Do not include any titles, headers, or other introductory text.

Hello... and welcome to the Austin Daily Brief, your essential guide to what's happening in the city. We've got a fantastic lineup of events for you this week, so let's get straight to it.

First up, we have [Event 1 Title].
(In a paragraph of 80-100 words, describe the event. Make it sound interesting and accessible. Cover the what, where, when, why it's cool, and cost/ticket info. **Incorporate 1-2 subtle audio tags or punctuation pauses.** For example: "It promises to be... [excitedly] an unforgettable experience.")

Next on the agenda, if you're a fan of [topic of Event 2, e.g., "local art" or "live music"], you are NOT going to want to miss [Event 2 Title].
(In a paragraph of 80-100 words, describe the event using the same guidelines as above. **Use tags or capitalization to add emphasis.** For example: "The best part? It's completely FREE.")

And finally, rounding out our week is [Event 3 Title].
(In a paragraph of 80-100 words, describe the event using the same guidelines as above. **Maybe use a tag to convey a specific feeling.** For example: "And for anyone who loves barbecue... [chuckles] well, you know what to do.")

That's the brief for this edition. You can find links and more details for everything mentioned in our show notes. Thanks for tuning in to the Austin Daily Brief, and [warmly] we'll see you next time.

## CONSTRAINTS ##

- **Total Script Word Count:** Keep the entire script between 350 and 450 words.
- **Tone:** Informative, friendly, clear, and efficient.
- **Audience Knowledge:** Assume the listener is familiar with major Austin landmarks and neighborhoods (e.g., Zilker Park, South Congress, East Austin). You don't need to give directions, just the location.
- **Output Format:** Generate *only* the dialogue for the script, beginning with "Hello...". The script must include embedded ElevenLabs v3 audio tags.

# Minister unveils tourism event calendar for Dakshina Kannada

## Minister unveils tourism event calendar for Dakshina Kannada


Mangalore Today News Network

**Mangaluru, July 7, 2024:** Minister for Health & Family Welfare, Dinesh Gundu Rao, unveiled a coastal tourism event calendar for Dakshina Kannada district at an event organized by the Coastal Karnataka Tourism Development Council on Saturday.

During his speech, the minister highlighted that this initiative marks the first step towards boosting tourism in the district. He noted that Dakshina Kannada has potential comparable to states like Goa and Kerala and emphasized the need to enhance facilities for both local and out-of-state tourists.

Stressing the importance of maintaining law and order for tourism growth, the minister assured that the government would provide the necessary support for the sector’s development. He also mentioned that the state government is open to welcoming private investments.

Lok Sabha member Capt. Brijesh Chowta, who launched the web portal at the event, described it as a significant move for promoting tourism in the district. He stated that the portal would help showcase the district’s culture and diverse activities to a broader audience, and that the central government would also work towards developing tourist spots in the area.

Deputy Commissioner Mullai Muhilan added that the Coastal Karnataka Tourism Development Council, in collaboration with the District Administration, aims to promote and enhance tourism in Dakshina Kannada. The event calendar features information about the district’s festivals and events throughout the year, which is expected to attract tourists year-round. He also mentioned that the web portal provides valuable information for tourists.

# Bajrang Dal leaders booked for inviting Sharan Pumpwell, violating event permission

The Mangaluru leader, facing earlier cases for provocative speeches, was allegedly given a platform at a Hiriyadka event.

[Naina J A](https://www.deccanherald.com/author/naina-j-a)

DHNS

Last Updated : 22 August 2025, 04:43 IST

Follow Us :

Mangaluru: A case has been registered at the Hiriyadka police station against [Bajrang Dal](https://www.deccanherald.com/search?q=bajrang%20dal) leaders for allegedly inviting [Sharan Pumpwell](https://www.deccanherald.com/search?q=sharan%20pumpwell), known for delivering provocative speeches in the past, to a programme without informing the police.

According to officials, the Hiriyadka unit of Bajrang Dal had organised a torchlight procession on August 20, scheduled from 6 pm between Kotnakatte and Devadiga Sabha Bhavan, followed by a public meeting.

However, the procession reportedly began at 7:30 pm, later than the permitted time, and the meeting continued at the Sabha Bhavan. Police said permission had been granted on the condition that no provocative speeches disturbing communal harmony would be allowed.

Despite this, it is alleged that rowdy-sheeter Dinesh Mendon and his associates invited Sharan Pumpwell of Mangaluru, already facing charges in a previous case involving inflammatory speeches, and gave him a platform. The meeting allegedly went on from 9 pm to 10 pm.

ADVERTISEMENT

The organisers, including Bajrang Dal leaders Dinesh Mendon and Subrahmanya Bhat, allegedly failed to inform the police about Pumpwell’s presence, leading to the case. Police have registered it under Section 105 of the Karnataka Police Act.

# Police file case against BJP, Congress leaders after clash at Mangaluru temple event

## An FIR has been registered against a BJP MLA from Mangaluru and 11 others over an alleged assault on a Congress worker during a temple event in the district. The clash erupted when Kamath confronted a Congress worker, leading to a scuffle between BJP and Congress supporters.

The police have registered an FIR against a local BJP MLA Vedavyas Kamath and 11 others following an alleged assault on a Congress worker during a religious event in Karnataka’s Mangaluru.

The incident, which occurred at Sri Krishna Bhajana Mandira near Shaktinagar in Mangalore City, late Sunday night (March 2) led to clashes between BJP and Congress workers.

According to a complaint filed by Congress worker Yashwanth Prabhu, the altercation began when the Mangalore City South MLA confronted him at the Brahma Kalashotsava ceremony, questioning his presence at the temple.

Prabhu alleged that the BJP leader remarked, “What work do you have here after throwing stones at temples?” a statement he perceived as politically charged. A verbal argument ensued, following which a group, including BJP workers, identified as Ashwith Kottari, Mani, and Jayaprakash, allegedly assaulted him and tore his shirt. Prabhu also claimed that Jayaprakash issued a life threat against him.

Following the complaint, BJP leader Mani R filed a counter-complaint, alleging that Congress workers attacked a BJP member from the Scheduled Caste community. BJP spokesperson Raj Gopal Rai dismissed the allegations against MLA Kamath as politically motivated, accusing Congress of creating a false narrative to target BJP leaders. He claimed that Congress workers attempted to provoke unrest at the event and later staged an attack to frame BJP leaders.

Police registered cases against members of both parties, and an investigation is underway.

The second edition of “Hombelaku Kreedotsava”, a sports and entertainment programme for elected members of gram panchayats and their staff in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts, will be held at Sahyadri Engineering College grounds in Mangaluru on February 22. The event is organised by Gram Swaraj Prathistana.

Taking to reporters here on Tuesday, Manjunath Bhandary, MLC, said the event will be for 6,082 panchayat members and more than 2,500 panchayat employees in the two coastal districts. The event will be held to being together the elected members and the staff, who work closely with people. Apart from various sports, they will be involved in different cultural competitions.

There will be parade of participants where they will display models related to themes namely ‘Nanna Kanasina Bharata’, ‘Gram Swaraj’, and ‘Karavali Samskruti’. The best marching contingent will receive prize money of ₹50,000, while the second team will get ₹25,000.

The sports will include volleyball and lemon and spoon competitions. There will also be group dance, patriotic song singing, folk dance, and other cultural competitions. The participants will be given t-shirts and food.

The State government had given ₹10 lakh to the event last year. The government has promised more funds for this year’s event. Mr. Bhandary said RDPR Minister Priyank Kharge and Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar have agreed to take part in the event.

\| Photo Credit: Special Arrangement


Swimmers from different swimming clubs of Dakshina Kannada dominated on the first of the two-day swimming events being held at Yemmekere Swimming Pool, on the fifth day of the Karnataka State Games 2025, in Mangaluru on Tuesday.

It started with Nishan from We One (WO) Aqua Centre, Mangaluru, who came third in the 1,500m freestyle for men with a time of 19:53.59 minutes. Dhruva B. from DKV Aquatic Centre of Bengaluru topped with 18:06.58 min, followed by Sachin Vishwanath from Global Swim Centre of Bengaluru with 19:02.53 min. In the 1,500m freestyle for women, Namratha Shetty from WO Mangaluru, the lone participant, covered the distance in 30:09.63 min.

Dhyaan M. from Global Swim Centre topped in 50m backstroke for men with 28.53 sec, followed by V.S. Diganth from Puttur Aquatic Club with 29.28 sec, followed by D. Gyan from Mangala Swimming Club of Mangaluru with 29.68 sec. Tanmayi Dharmesh from Global Swim Centre topped in 50m backstroke for women with 33.73 sec, followed by Pradhi Clare Pinto (35.55 sec) and Prateeksha N. Shenoy (38.09 sec), both from Puttur Aquatic Club.

In the 100m backstroke for men, O.R. Surya Jhoyappa from Basavanagudi Aquatic Centre topped with 1:12.46 min, followed by Nishan (1:16:90 min) and Alaister Samuel Rego (1:17.58 min), both from WO Mangaluru. It was all swimmers of Dakshina Kannada in 100m backstroke for women with S.R. Rachana Rao topping with 1:20.65 min, followed by Rianna Dhrithi Fernandes (1:20.84 min), both from WO Mangaluru, and Prateeksha N. Shenoy of Puttur Aquatic Club (1:25.91 min).

M. Harshavardhan of Global Swim Centre topped in the 200m butterfly for men with 2:24.90 min, followed by Steve Jeff Lobo of WO Mangaluru (2:42.35 min) and Ethan Paul Mascarenhas of Jai Hind Swimming Club (3:52.97 min).

In the 200m freestyle for men, national swimmer from Mangaluru Chinthan S. Shetty, who swam for Lakshan Academy of Bengaluru, topped with 2:00.90 min, followed by N. Dhoneesh of Vijayanagar Aquatic Centre (2:03.47 min) and Alaister Samuel Rego from WO Mangaluru (2:03.59 min). In 200m freestyle for women, Pradhi Clare Pinto topped with 2:41.37 min, followed by U. Anikha (3:10.36 min), both from Puttur Aquatic Club, and Namratha Shetty of WO Mangaluru (3:39.55 min).

In the team events, WO Mangaluru team stood first in the 4X100m freestyle relay with 3:55.18 min, followed by Puttur Aquatic Club (4:00.15 min) and Basavanagudi Aquatic Centre (4:03.45 min). The WO Mangaluru A team stood first in the 4X100m medley with 5:28.08, followed by WO Mangaluru B team with 6:04.51 min.

As many as 65 of the 80 swimmers from aquatic clubs of the State are participating in the swimming competition. Some of the best swimmers of the State are not participating as they are set to take part in the National Swimming Championship to be held in Jharkhand in the last week of January.

Speaker U.T. Khader released the invitation for the 27th Dakshina Kannada District Kannada Sahitya Sammelana which will be held at Mangalore University’s Mangala auditorium for two days from February 21, at the university on February 12.
\| Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRAGEMENT


Legislative Assembly Speaker U.T. Khader said on Wednesday, February 12, that literary conferences helped in promoting Kannada and culture.

He was addressing a gathering at Mangalore University after releasing the invitation for the 27th Dakshina Kannada District Kannada Sahitya Sammelana which will be held at the university’s Mangala auditorium for two days from February 21.

Mr. Khader said that more school students, writers, and other people in general should participate in the conference which should be organised in such a way that it should emerge as a model for the State.

Dhananjaya Kumble, the conference committee’s secretary, said that the conference will be organised by Dakshina Kannada District Sahitya Parishat and the university. In all, 18 books by various authors will be released during the conference.

A cultural exhibition showcasing the district’s cultural heritage will be held on the occasion. The exhibition will feature book stalls, food stalls, and other attractions, Mr. Kumble said.

Processions will be held from the nearby villages to the venue to promote Kannada language and culture. The conference aims to promote Kannada language and culture among the people, especially the younger generation, he said.

K. Raju Mogaveera, the university’s Registrar (administration), Sadashiva Ullal, president, Mangaluru Urban Development Authority and Mamata Gatti, chairperson, Karnataka Cashew Development Corporation were present.

Mangaluru: Aati is not just about preparing and enjoying various delicacies; instead, efforts should be made to comprehend its genuine significance and true form, said Athrady Amrutha Shetty, a member of the Dr Shivaram Karanth Trust. She spoke about Aati during the ‘Aatida Gena' event organised by the Karnataka Tulu Sahitya Academy and the women's wing of the All India Mundala Youth Forum at the Tulu Bhavana on Sunday.She stressed the importance of understanding the challenges associated with the Aati month. Although such issues may not be prevalent now, future generations should be aware of them. It is crucial to understand the reasons and effects of consuming Aati Kashaya. Aati is not an inauspicious time; it is a month of well-being and happiness. It is a time to demonstrate and prove the strength of Tulu women and their ability to manage household responsibilities.One should recognise the care and values of life that she embodies by feeding both her family and guests, she added.The food consumed during the rainy season is more about sustenance than taste. Aati Kashaya was an integral part of life for previous generations, but now it has become a trend on social media, she noted.

Tharanath Gatti Kapikad, chairman of the Karnataka Tulu Sahitya Academy, said that Aati should not be limited to playing in the paddy fields' mud. Instead, we should cultivate the desire to grow rice at least once a year and focus on reviving cultivation in fallow fields, he said.Dr Kalpana Ashfaque, associate professor, department of physiology, AJ Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Centre, inaugurated the event.

Team Karnataka at the first National Sea Kayaking and Stand-Up Paddling Championship-2023 held in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu, recently.
\| Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT


Team Karnataka, under the leadership of Udupi-based Rohan R. Suvarna and comprising seven members, bagged nine medals in the recently concluded National Sea Kayaking and Stand-Up Paddling Championship-2023 at Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu.

The championship, conducted for the first time, was organised by the Indian Kayaking and Canoeing Association. The Karnataka team bagged the medals in various events. Sinchana D. Gowda achieved an impressive feat, clinching four gold medals (one in the individual category and three in doubles), one silver, and four bronze medals. Anne Mathias secured three gold medals in the doubles category. Tharuna Kumar B.R. and M. Manjunatha Naik jointly won the bronze medal in the doubles category.

Karnataka team’s exceptional performance led the team to emerge as the runner-up champion. Dileep Kumar, secretary, Karnataka Canoeing and Kayaking Association, supported the athletes throughout this event.

**Mangaluru:** As the 11th International Yoga Day is being celebrated with much fanfare everywhere on Saturday, the coastal city of Mangaluru celebrated the occasion with a distinctive aquatic twist - through Jala yoga, or water yoga.

Held at the Mangaluru City Corporation Swimming Pool, the event saw around 40 members of an amateur swimmers' group perform yoga postures such as Padmasana and Shavasana while floating in 16-feet-deep water.

The organisers of the event highlighted how water yoga 'a blend of traditional yoga postures, breathing techniques, and meditation practiced in water' can enhance both physical fitness and mental relaxation.

Adding a creative note to the celebrations, retired Dean of the Mangalore University of Fisheries, S M Shivaprakash, wrote a postcard to Prime Minister Narendra Modi while swimming.

"Dear Modiji, Happy International Yoga Day. I am writing this postcard while swimming in the pool. Fit India -- Shivaprakash, Mangaluru," read the handwritten note that drew attention at the event.

Also Read - [read-media](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/karnataka/shivakumar-offers-apology-over-rss-prayer-row-reaffirms-loyalty-to-congress-1899797)[Shivakumar Offers Apology Over RSS Prayer Row, Reaffirms Loyalty to Congress](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/karnataka/shivakumar-offers-apology-over-rss-prayer-row-reaffirms-loyalty-to-congress-1899797)

Speaking to reporters, Shivaprakash said, "Prime Minister Modi has taken yoga to the global stage. Yoga is about harmony between the body, mind, and soul. I swim daily, and today I wanted to honour Yoga Day in my own way."

The event was organised by the amateur swimmers' group in collaboration with the city's public swimming pool, under the theme of this year's Yoga Day: One Earth, One Health.

One of the participants, Chandrahass Shetty, said it was the first time such an aquatic yoga demonstration had been attempted in the city.

Also Read - [read-media](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/karnataka/karnataka-guv-presents-namma-bengaluru-awards-to-citys-top-contributors-1899784)[Karnataka Guv Presents 'Namma Bengaluru Awards' To City's Top Contributors](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/karnataka/karnataka-guv-presents-namma-bengaluru-awards-to-citys-top-contributors-1899784)

Participants reported feeling lighter and more flexible while performing asanas in water, attributing it to reduced pressure on the muscles. They also noted that the buoyancy made it easier to maintain poses for longer durations.

The event, blending physical discipline with creativity and environmental awareness, offered a fresh perspective on yoga and its adaptability. Organisers said the event is aimed at promoting a healthy lifestyle and demonstrating India's evolving innovations in wellness practices.

The India Paddle Festival 2025, India’s sole international Stand-Up Paddle (SUP) event, was inaugurated by Priyank Kharge, Minister of Rural Development & Panchayat Raj, IT & BT, at a function at Sahyadri Campus on Saturday.

Hosted by Incredible India and Karnataka Tourism, the festival released its official creatives alongside a promotional video of its inaugural success.Scheduled from March 7 to 9 at Sasihithlu Beach, the India Paddle Festival 2025 aims to position stand-up paddleboarding and surfing tourism while carving Karnataka’s shoreline into a leading destination in water sports globally.

## **India Paddle Festival 2025: Encouraging Adventure Tourism In Karnataka**

>
> [A post shared by Surfing Swami Foundation (@surfingswamifoundation)](https://www.instagram.com/p/DGYDnefSXoG/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

Addressing the launch, Minister Priyank Kharge underlined the festival’s contribution towards developing adventure tourism in Karnataka. ‘Karnataka’s beautiful coastline is the ideal backdrop for international competitions such as this.

The state’s rapid development of coastal sports, particularly surfing and stand-up paddleboarding, is quite impressive. We continue to support efforts that promote adventure tourism and local sports,’ he stated.

The event is being hosted by the Surfing Swami Foundation and will include top international paddlers from the Association of Paddle Surf Professionals World Tour, along with up-and-coming Indian players competing on an international level.

Ram Mohan Paranjape, head of the Surfing Swami Foundation, highlighted the India Paddle Festival 2025 as a platform for sustainable growth and the development of water sports in India. “With top-level competitions, mass events, and workshops, the festival will fill an action-packed calendar and place India on the map for SUP,” he further added.

Through the fusion of competitive and community events, the India Paddle Festival 2025 is likely to attract major international players, adventure sports enthusiasts, and tourist attention, further cementing India’s status as a leading player in the sport of stand-up paddleboarding.

Whether you are a sportsperson, a water sports athlete, or a simple person seeking an experience unlike any other near the sea, there is something for everyone in this festival.

Thousands of devotees are expected to take part in the dasara and Navarathri celebrations. The temple has made all the arrangements for celebrations, Sairam told mediapersons on Monday.

The Dasara Mahotsav will begin with the guru puja celebrations followed by various rituals.

Treasurer Padmaraj R said that rituals like _Durga homa_ (Oct 4), _Panchadurga homa_ (Oct 5), _Arya Durga homa_ (Oct 6), _Ambika Durga Homa_ (Oct 7), _Bhagavathi Durga homa_ (Oct 8), _Chandika homa_ (Oct 9), _Mahishamardini Durga homa_ (Oct 10), _Chandika homa hagalotsava_ (Oct 11), _Saraswati Durga homa_ (Oct 12), _Vageshwari Durga homa_ (Oct 13) will be held.

The grand 'dasara' procession will be held on October 13 with the procession of idols of Mahaganapathi, Navadurge, Sharada and colourful tableaus and art teams. The idols will be immersed in the temple lake in the wee hours of October 14. Kerala chende, folk teams, dance troupes, dola dance by Maharashtrian artistes, Kalladka Gombe, colourful umbrellas from Thrissur, tiger dance, tableaux of various temples will add colours to the procession, he said.

**Auction of stalls**

To a query on auction of stalls by the Mangaluru City Corporation, Padmaraj said, “The High Court has directed the MCC to follow the due procedure while auctioning stalls during temple fairs. Accordingly, the MCC has decided to auction the stalls. However, the temple committee has urged the Deputy Commissioner and MCC Commissioner not to allot stalls inside the arch leading to the temple and in temple premises. Allowing the traders to set up stalls inside the arch will cause inconvenience to the devotees especially senior citizens visiting the temple.”

**Half marathon**

As a part of 'dasara' celebrations, a half marathon covering 21-km will be organised on October 6 at 5.30 am. About 1,500 to 2,000 people are likely to take part in the half marathon. Last year, a walkathon was organised, said Padmaraj.

Cultural programmes will be held daily from 6 pm at the temple premises, he added.

# Mangaluru Dasara Event From September 26, 10 lakh People Expected To Attend

## More than 10 lakh people from various districts are expected to arrive in the city for the celebrations and preparations are on to hold the festival on a grand scale, said B Janaradhan Poojary.

The Mangaluru Dasara festival will be celebrated at the Kudroli Gokarnanatha temple.

**Mangaluru, Karnataka:**

The Mangaluru Dasara festival will be celebrated at the Kudroli Gokarnanatha temple from September 26 to October 6, former Union Minister B Janaradhan Poojary, patron of the temple, has said.

This year's celebrations will be unique as the festival could not be held during the previous two years on account of the Covid-19 pandemic, he told reporters here yesterday.

More than 10 lakh people from various districts of the state are expected to arrive in the city for the celebrations and preparations are on to hold the festival on a grand scale, he said.

Religious rituals will be held every day and food will be served to devotees. It is proposed to hold 'Chandika Yaga' in the glass house for the convenience of devotees, Mr Poojary said.

Mr Poojary said he will personally invite Chief Minister Basavaraj Bommai to inaugurate the festivities. The timing will be confirmed depending on the availability of the chief minister, he added.

Temple treasurer R Padmaraj said a silver pedestal weighing 12 kg for Goddess Sharada, being made at a cost of Rs 12 lakh, will be offered on September 24. A family of devotees will be offering a silver veena to the temple.

Certain changes have been made in the holding of the Dasara procession as per the convenience of devotees, he said.

Kudla Pili Parba 2024 season-3, organised by the Kudla Cultural Foundation, under the guidance of former MP Nalin Kumar Kateel, and the leadership of MLA D Vedavyas Kamath, ended at the Nehru Maidan on Friday late night.

In a fierce competition between 10 teams, Mulihithlu Friends Circle won the crown of Pili Parba 2024. The second prize was claimed by the Puraldappena Mokeda Bollilu Polali Tigers, while the Nandigudde Friends Babugudde and Team Kallega Tigers Puttur teams shared the third spot.

Among the special prizes, Talent Tigers Tulunadu team won 'Kappu Pili' (Black Tiger) award, while Mulihithlu Friends Circle team bagged 'Mari Huli' (cub Tiger) award. The most anticipated 'Parbada Pili' (Tiger of the Festival), was awarded to Team Kallega Tigers Puttur.

Team Parashurama Kudla was recognised as the most disciplined team. The second prize in the painting and procession category was won by SKB Tigers Kumpala.

Nandigudde Friends Babugudde won the prize in the Mudi category (rice wrapped in straws, weighing 42-kg thrown with the help of teeth), while MFT Mulihithlu secured the first place in the 'Dharani Mandala' and procession category.

In the himmela music category, the Puraldappena Mokeda Bollilu Polali Tigers took home the prize. All participating teams were felicitated with consolation awards.

During the inauguration of the Pili parba, Dakshin Kannada MP Capt Brijesh Chowta said Tuluva culture was the uniqueness of the district. "Let us all work towards saving the culture and tradition of the land."

Film actors Rishab Shetty, Raj B Shetty, DK BJP president Sathish Kumpala, Mayor Manoj Kodikal, SCDCC president Rajendra Kumar and others were present.

The Karnataka State Olympics Association will host the State Olympics in Udupi and Mangaluru, beginning on January 17. The event will include over 11 sports such as athletics, judo, and kayaking, with facilities being reviewed to accommodate the 2,500 participating athletes and officials.

UDUPI: The Karnataka State Olympics Association will organise the State Olympics in Udupi and Mangaluru. MLA Yashpal Suvarna and deputy commissioner Vidya Kumari K conducted an inspection at the Ajjarkad District Stadium on Wednesday to review arrangements, including ground facilities, athlete accommodations, and other requirements for the event scheduled in Udupi city.

Deputy commissioner Vidya Kumari said that more than 11 events will be held in Udupi over eight days starting from Jan 17. Athletics, judo, wrestling, boxing, kabaddi, and cycling will take place at the Ajjarkad District Stadium, while MAHE's sports grounds will host table tennis and hockey events.

Kayaking will be conducted in the Swarna River at Baikady, Brahmavar. Over 2,500 athletes are expected to participate, and plans are being drawn up to ensure the events are conducted in an organised and disciplined manner.

MLA Yashpal Suvarna said that all arrangements for athletes, referees, officials, and other participants must be undertaken. Facilities for accommodation, food, transportation, and other basic amenities should be prepared well in advance to ensure the smooth conduct of the games.

Superintendent of police Dr. Arun K, chief planning officer of the Zilla Panchayat Uday Kumar Shetty, assistant director of youth empowerment and sports Roshan Kumar Shetty, Backward Classes Welfare officer Hakappa R. Lamani, ITDP planning coordinator Narayana Swamy, and other officials were present.

Hello... and welcome to the Austin Daily Brief, your essential guide to what's happening in the city. We've got a fantastic lineup of events for you this week, so let's get straight to it.

First up, we have **Aqua Flow Yoga** happening at the Deep Eddy Pool. Imagine yourself... [peacefully] floating and stretching in the refreshing spring-fed waters, performing gentle poses like a serene 'Floating Lotus' or a relaxing 'Water Shavasana'. This unique event, inspired by the calming practice of Jala Yoga, offers a fantastic way to combine physical fitness with deep mental relaxation. It's perfect for all skill levels, providing buoyancy that supports your joints and enhances flexibility. Join dozens of fellow Austinites on Saturday, July 20th, from 9 AM to 11 AM. Tickets are just $15, and it’s a wonderful way to find your zen... [calmly] right in the heart of the city.

Next on the agenda, if you're a fan of **Austin's beautiful waterways**, you are NOT going to want to miss the **Lake Travis Paddle Fest**! Get ready for a weekend of exhilarating stand-up paddleboarding and kayaking competitions on Lake Travis. Happening from August 9th to 11th at Mansfield Dam Park, this festival welcomes both seasoned athletes and enthusiastic beginners. Watch international paddle pros demonstrate incredible skill, or sign up for one of the community races. There will also be workshops for those looking to try SUP for the first time. It's a fantastic way to experience the lake, enjoy live music, and soak up the sun. Registration fees vary by event, starting at $30, and spectators are... [excitedly] absolutely FREE!

And finally, rounding out our week is the vibrant **East Austin Heritage Fiesta**! This lively community event celebrates Austin's rich cultural tapestry with a focus on local art, music, and of course... [chuckles] delicious food. Head over to the historic Huston-Tillotson University campus on Saturday, September 7th, from 11 AM to 6 PM. You'll find a bustling marketplace with local artisans, live performances showcasing diverse dance and musical traditions, and an array of food trucks serving up authentic Austin flavors. There will even be a fun 'Community Games' area for all ages. It's a FREE, family-friendly event designed to bring everyone together and enjoy the very best of East Austin's spirit. A perfect weekend outing!

That's the brief for this edition. You can find links and more details for everything mentioned in our show notes. Thanks for tuning in to the Austin Daily Brief, and [warmly] we'll see you next time.

# Minister unveils tourism event calendar for Dakshina Kannada

## Minister unveils tourism event calendar for Dakshina Kannada


Mangalore Today News Network

**Mangaluru, July 7, 2024:** Minister for Health & Family Welfare, Dinesh Gundu Rao, unveiled a coastal tourism event calendar for Dakshina Kannada district at an event organized by the Coastal Karnataka Tourism Development Council on Saturday.

During his speech, the minister highlighted that this initiative marks the first step towards boosting tourism in the district. He noted that Dakshina Kannada has potential comparable to states like Goa and Kerala and emphasized the need to enhance facilities for both local and out-of-state tourists.

Stressing the importance of maintaining law and order for tourism growth, the minister assured that the government would provide the necessary support for the sector’s development. He also mentioned that the state government is open to welcoming private investments.

Lok Sabha member Capt. Brijesh Chowta, who launched the web portal at the event, described it as a significant move for promoting tourism in the district. He stated that the portal would help showcase the district’s culture and diverse activities to a broader audience, and that the central government would also work towards developing tourist spots in the area.

Deputy Commissioner Mullai Muhilan added that the Coastal Karnataka Tourism Development Council, in collaboration with the District Administration, aims to promote and enhance tourism in Dakshina Kannada. The event calendar features information about the district’s festivals and events throughout the year, which is expected to attract tourists year-round. He also mentioned that the web portal provides valuable information for tourists.

# Bajrang Dal leaders booked for inviting Sharan Pumpwell, violating event permission

The Mangaluru leader, facing earlier cases for provocative speeches, was allegedly given a platform at a Hiriyadka event.

[Naina J A](https://www.deccanherald.com/author/naina-j-a)

DHNS

Last Updated : 22 August 2025, 04:43 IST

Follow Us :

0

Sharan Pumpwell.

Credit: DH Photo

Mangaluru: A case has been registered at the Hiriyadka police station against [Bajrang Dal](https://www.deccanherald.com/search?q=bajrang%20dal) leaders for allegedly inviting [Sharan Pumpwell](https://www.deccanherald.com/search?q=sharan%20pumpwell), known for delivering provocative speeches in the past, to a programme without informing the police.

Addas your preferred

news source on Google

Add Now

ADVERTISEMENT

ADVERTISEMENT

According to officials, the Hiriyadka unit of Bajrang Dal had organised a torchlight procession on August 20, scheduled from 6 pm between Kotnakatte and Devadiga Sabha Bhavan, followed by a public meeting.

However, the procession reportedly began at 7:30 pm, later than the permitted time, and the meeting continued at the Sabha Bhavan. Police said permission had been granted on the condition that no provocative speeches disturbing communal harmony would be allowed.

Despite this, it is alleged that rowdy-sheeter Dinesh Mendon and his associates invited Sharan Pumpwell of Mangaluru, already facing charges in a previous case involving inflammatory speeches, and gave him a platform. The meeting allegedly went on from 9 pm to 10 pm.

ADVERTISEMENT

The organisers, including Bajrang Dal leaders Dinesh Mendon and Subrahmanya Bhat, allegedly failed to inform the police about Pumpwell’s presence, leading to the case. Police have registered it under Section 105 of the Karnataka Police Act.

# Police file case against BJP, Congress leaders after clash at Mangaluru temple event

## An FIR has been registered against a BJP MLA from Mangaluru and 11 others over an alleged assault on a Congress worker during a temple event in the district. The clash erupted when Kamath confronted a Congress worker, leading to a scuffle between BJP and Congress supporters.

Police file case against BJP MLA Vedavyas Kamath after alleged attack on Congress leader Yashwanth Prabhu (right) at temple fest.

[Sagay Raj](https://www.indiatoday.in/author/sagay-raj-0 "Sagay Raj")

[Sagay Raj](https://www.indiatoday.in/author/sagay-raj-0 "Sagay Raj") [Sagay Raj](https://twitter.com/@sagayrajp "Sagay Raj")

UPDATED:Mar 4, 2025 13:27 IST

Written By: [Deepthi Rao](https://www.indiatoday.in/author/deepthi-narayan-rao)

The police have registered an FIR against a local BJP MLA Vedavyas Kamath and 11 others following an alleged assault on a Congress worker during a religious event in Karnataka’s Mangaluru.

The incident, which occurred at Sri Krishna Bhajana Mandira near Shaktinagar in Mangalore City, late Sunday night (March 2) led to clashes between BJP and Congress workers.

preferred source

[Add India Today As A Trusted Source](https://intdy.in/itprfd "Trusted Source")

advertisement

According to a complaint filed by Congress worker Yashwanth Prabhu, the altercation began when the Mangalore City South MLA confronted him at the Brahma Kalashotsava ceremony, questioning his presence at the temple.

Prabhu alleged that the BJP leader remarked, “What work do you have here after throwing stones at temples?” a statement he perceived as politically charged. A verbal argument ensued, following which a group, including BJP workers, identified as Ashwith Kottari, Mani, and Jayaprakash, allegedly assaulted him and tore his shirt. Prabhu also claimed that Jayaprakash issued a life threat against him.

Following the complaint, BJP leader Mani R filed a counter-complaint, alleging that Congress workers attacked a BJP member from the Scheduled Caste community. BJP spokesperson Raj Gopal Rai dismissed the allegations against MLA Kamath as politically motivated, accusing Congress of creating a false narrative to target BJP leaders. He claimed that Congress workers attempted to provoke unrest at the event and later staged an attack to frame BJP leaders.

Police registered cases against members of both parties, and an investigation is underway.

# Second edition of Hombelaku Kreedotsava to be held in Mangaluru on February 22

Published \- February 04, 2025 10:31 pm IST - Mangaluru

[The Hindu Bureau](https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/The-Hindu-Bureau-14355/)

0

READ LATER

Remove
[SEE ALL](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks)

PRINT

Manjunath Bhandarym MLC, along with office-bearers of Hombelaku Sangatana Samiti releasing a poster of Hombelaku event in Mangaluru on Tuesday.
\| Photo Credit: H.S. MANJUNATH


The second edition of “Hombelaku Kreedotsava”, a sports and entertainment programme for elected members of gram panchayats and their staff in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts, will be held at Sahyadri Engineering College grounds in Mangaluru on February 22. The event is organised by Gram Swaraj Prathistana.

Taking to reporters here on Tuesday, Manjunath Bhandary, MLC, said the event will be for 6,082 panchayat members and more than 2,500 panchayat employees in the two coastal districts. The event will be held to being together the elected members and the staff, who work closely with people. Apart from various sports, they will be involved in different cultural competitions.

There will be parade of participants where they will display models related to themes namely ‘Nanna Kanasina Bharata’, ‘Gram Swaraj’, and ‘Karavali Samskruti’. The best marching contingent will receive prize money of ₹50,000, while the second team will get ₹25,000.

The sports will include volleyball and lemon and spoon competitions. There will also be group dance, patriotic song singing, folk dance, and other cultural competitions. The participants will be given t-shirts and food.

The State government had given ₹10 lakh to the event last year. The government has promised more funds for this year’s event. Mr. Bhandary said RDPR Minister Priyank Kharge and Deputy Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar have agreed to take part in the event.

# Four from Karnataka to take part in sailing event

Published \- April 16, 2025 09:27 pm IST - MANGALURU

[The Hindu Bureau](https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/The-Hindu-Bureau-14355/)

The four children from Karnataka selected to take part in the ‘Youth Nationals’ sailing event to be held in Mumbai. Also seen are members of Coastal Karnataka Sailing Club.
\| Photo Credit: Special Arrangement


Four children from Karnataka, including two from Mangaluru, will take part in the ‘Youth Nationals’ sailing event to be conducted by Yachting Association of India in Marve, Mumbai, from May 3 to 10.

In a press release, the Mangaluru-based Coastal Karnataka Sailing Club identified the children as K.A. Vaishnav. 9, from BGS School Mangaluru; Kane Veyon, 9, Mount Carmel Central School, Mangaluru; Kevin Saha, 10, from Brigade School, Malleswaram, Bengaluru, and Bhuvisutha La Indian, 11, from Manasarowar Pushkarini Vidyashrama, Mysuru.

These four were selected from a total of 15 students who attended the Summer Sailing Camp Talent Hunt, organised by the Sailing Club in Phalguni (Gurupura) River near Kuloor bridge, Mangaluru, between April 5 and 14. Team coach J. Yashwanth Gowda said this was the first time a Karnataka team would participate in the Youth Nationals event.

The club thanked the Department of Youth Services and Sports and CodeCraft Technologies for their support.

# Karnataka State Games 2025: DK swimmers dominate in swimming events

## As many as 65 of the 80 swimmers from aquatic clubs in Karnataka are participating in the swimming competition

Updated  \- January 22, 2025 10:57 am IST - MANGALURU

[The Hindu Bureau](https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/The-Hindu-Bureau-14355/)

0 / 0 New

READ LATER

Remove
[SEE ALL](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks)

PRINT

Swimmers from Dakshina Kannada dominated on the first day of two-day swimming events, in the ongoing Karnataka State Games 2025, at the Yemmekere Swimming pool in Mangaluru on Tuesday.
\| Photo Credit: Special Arrangement


Swimmers from different swimming clubs of Dakshina Kannada dominated on the first of the two-day swimming events being held at Yemmekere Swimming Pool, on the fifth day of the Karnataka State Games 2025, in Mangaluru on Tuesday.

It started with Nishan from We One (WO) Aqua Centre, Mangaluru, who came third in the 1,500m freestyle for men with a time of 19:53.59 minutes. Dhruva B. from DKV Aquatic Centre of Bengaluru topped with 18:06.58 min, followed by Sachin Vishwanath from Global Swim Centre of Bengaluru with 19:02.53 min. In the 1,500m freestyle for women, Namratha Shetty from WO Mangaluru, the lone participant, covered the distance in 30:09.63 min.

Dhyaan M. from Global Swim Centre topped in 50m backstroke for men with 28.53 sec, followed by V.S. Diganth from Puttur Aquatic Club with 29.28 sec, followed by D. Gyan from Mangala Swimming Club of Mangaluru with 29.68 sec. Tanmayi Dharmesh from Global Swim Centre topped in 50m backstroke for women with 33.73 sec, followed by Pradhi Clare Pinto (35.55 sec) and Prateeksha N. Shenoy (38.09 sec), both from Puttur Aquatic Club.

In the 100m backstroke for men, O.R. Surya Jhoyappa from Basavanagudi Aquatic Centre topped with 1:12.46 min, followed by Nishan (1:16:90 min) and Alaister Samuel Rego (1:17.58 min), both from WO Mangaluru. It was all swimmers of Dakshina Kannada in 100m backstroke for women with S.R. Rachana Rao topping with 1:20.65 min, followed by Rianna Dhrithi Fernandes (1:20.84 min), both from WO Mangaluru, and Prateeksha N. Shenoy of Puttur Aquatic Club (1:25.91 min).

M. Harshavardhan of Global Swim Centre topped in the 200m butterfly for men with 2:24.90 min, followed by Steve Jeff Lobo of WO Mangaluru (2:42.35 min) and Ethan Paul Mascarenhas of Jai Hind Swimming Club (3:52.97 min).

In the 200m freestyle for men, national swimmer from Mangaluru Chinthan S. Shetty, who swam for Lakshan Academy of Bengaluru, topped with 2:00.90 min, followed by N. Dhoneesh of Vijayanagar Aquatic Centre (2:03.47 min) and Alaister Samuel Rego from WO Mangaluru (2:03.59 min). In 200m freestyle for women, Pradhi Clare Pinto topped with 2:41.37 min, followed by U. Anikha (3:10.36 min), both from Puttur Aquatic Club, and Namratha Shetty of WO Mangaluru (3:39.55 min).

In the team events, WO Mangaluru team stood first in the 4X100m freestyle relay with 3:55.18 min, followed by Puttur Aquatic Club (4:00.15 min) and Basavanagudi Aquatic Centre (4:03.45 min). The WO Mangaluru A team stood first in the 4X100m medley with 5:28.08, followed by WO Mangaluru B team with 6:04.51 min.

As many as 65 of the 80 swimmers from aquatic clubs of the State are participating in the swimming competition. Some of the best swimmers of the State are not participating as they are set to take part in the National Swimming Championship to be held in Jharkhand in the last week of January.

# Literary events helped in promoting Kannada and culture, says U. T. Khader

Published \- February 12, 2025 07:31 pm IST - MANGALURU

[The Hindu Bureau](https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/The-Hindu-Bureau-14355/)

0

READ LATER

[SEE ALL](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks)

Speaker U.T. Khader released the invitation for the 27th Dakshina Kannada District Kannada Sahitya Sammelana which will be held at Mangalore University’s Mangala auditorium for two days from February 21, at the university on February 12.
\| Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRAGEMENT


Legislative Assembly Speaker U.T. Khader said on Wednesday, February 12, that literary conferences helped in promoting Kannada and culture.

He was addressing a gathering at Mangalore University after releasing the invitation for the 27th Dakshina Kannada District Kannada Sahitya Sammelana which will be held at the university’s Mangala auditorium for two days from February 21.

Mr. Khader said that more school students, writers, and other people in general should participate in the conference which should be organised in such a way that it should emerge as a model for the State.

Dhananjaya Kumble, the conference committee’s secretary, said that the conference will be organised by Dakshina Kannada District Sahitya Parishat and the university. In all, 18 books by various authors will be released during the conference.

A cultural exhibition showcasing the district’s cultural heritage will be held on the occasion. The exhibition will feature book stalls, food stalls, and other attractions, Mr. Kumble said.

Processions will be held from the nearby villages to the venue to promote Kannada language and culture. The conference aims to promote Kannada language and culture among the people, especially the younger generation, he said.

K. Raju Mogaveera, the university’s Registrar (administration), Sadashiva Ullal, president, Mangaluru Urban Development Authority and Mamata Gatti, chairperson, Karnataka Cashew Development Corporation were present.

# Aatida Gena event held

TNN /  Aug 03, 2025, 22:53 IST

Share

[print article](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshowprint/123079393.cms "print article")

AA

+ **Text Size**

- Small
- Medium
- Large

Mangaluru: Aati is not just about preparing and enjoying various delicacies; instead, efforts should be made to comprehend its genuine significance and true form, said Athrady Amrutha Shetty, a member of the Dr Shivaram Karanth Trust. She spoke about Aati during the ‘Aatida Gena' event organised by the Karnataka Tulu Sahitya Academy and the women's wing of the All India Mundala Youth Forum at the Tulu Bhavana on Sunday.She stressed the importance of understanding the challenges associated with the Aati month. Although such issues may not be prevalent now, future generations should be aware of them. It is crucial to understand the reasons and effects of consuming Aati Kashaya. Aati is not an inauspicious time; it is a month of well-being and happiness. It is a time to demonstrate and prove the strength of Tulu women and their ability to manage household responsibilities.One should recognise the care and values of life that she embodies by feeding both her family and guests, she added.The food consumed during the rainy season is more about sustenance than taste. Aati Kashaya was an integral part of life for previous generations, but now it has become a trend on social media, she noted.

Tharanath Gatti Kapikad, chairman of the Karnataka Tulu Sahitya Academy, said that Aati should not be limited to playing in the paddy fields' mud. Instead, we should cultivate the desire to grow rice at least once a year and focus on reviving cultivation in fallow fields, he said.Dr Kalpana Ashfaque, associate professor, department of physiology, AJ Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Centre, inaugurated the event.

# Karnataka team wins nine medals in National Sea Kayaking and Stand-Up Paddling event

Updated  \- September 21, 2023 09:46 pm IST - MANGALURU

[The Hindu Bureau](https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/The-Hindu-Bureau-14355/)

0

READ LATER

Team Karnataka at the first National Sea Kayaking and Stand-Up Paddling Championship-2023 held in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu, recently.
\| Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT


Team Karnataka, under the leadership of Udupi-based Rohan R. Suvarna and comprising seven members, bagged nine medals in the recently concluded National Sea Kayaking and Stand-Up Paddling Championship-2023 at Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu.

The championship, conducted for the first time, was organised by the Indian Kayaking and Canoeing Association. The Karnataka team bagged the medals in various events. Sinchana D. Gowda achieved an impressive feat, clinching four gold medals (one in the individual category and three in doubles), one silver, and four bronze medals. Anne Mathias secured three gold medals in the doubles category. Tharuna Kumar B.R. and M. Manjunatha Naik jointly won the bronze medal in the doubles category.

Karnataka team’s exceptional performance led the team to emerge as the runner-up champion. Dileep Kumar, secretary, Karnataka Canoeing and Kayaking Association, supported the athletes throughout this event.

# Mangaluru Hosts Unique 'Jala yoga' Event In Swimming Pool

[Karnataka](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/karnataka)

## The organisers of the event highlighted how water yoga 'a blend of traditional yoga postures, breathing techniques, and meditation practiced in water' can enhance both physical fitness and mental relaxation

**Mangaluru:** As the 11th International Yoga Day is being celebrated with much fanfare everywhere on Saturday, the coastal city of Mangaluru celebrated the occasion with a distinctive aquatic twist - through Jala yoga, or water yoga.

Held at the Mangaluru City Corporation Swimming Pool, the event saw around 40 members of an amateur swimmers' group perform yoga postures such as Padmasana and Shavasana while floating in 16-feet-deep water.

The organisers of the event highlighted how water yoga 'a blend of traditional yoga postures, breathing techniques, and meditation practiced in water' can enhance both physical fitness and mental relaxation.

Adding a creative note to the celebrations, retired Dean of the Mangalore University of Fisheries, S M Shivaprakash, wrote a postcard to Prime Minister Narendra Modi while swimming.

"Dear Modiji, Happy International Yoga Day. I am writing this postcard while swimming in the pool. Fit India -- Shivaprakash, Mangaluru," read the handwritten note that drew attention at the event.

Also Read - [read-media](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/karnataka/shivakumar-offers-apology-over-rss-prayer-row-reaffirms-loyalty-to-congress-1899797)[Shivakumar Offers Apology Over RSS Prayer Row, Reaffirms Loyalty to Congress](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/karnataka/shivakumar-offers-apology-over-rss-prayer-row-reaffirms-loyalty-to-congress-1899797)

Speaking to reporters, Shivaprakash said, "Prime Minister Modi has taken yoga to the global stage. Yoga is about harmony between the body, mind, and soul. I swim daily, and today I wanted to honour Yoga Day in my own way."

The event was organised by the amateur swimmers' group in collaboration with the city's public swimming pool, under the theme of this year's Yoga Day: One Earth, One Health.

One of the participants, Chandrahass Shetty, said it was the first time such an aquatic yoga demonstration had been attempted in the city.

Also Read - [read-media](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/karnataka/karnataka-guv-presents-namma-bengaluru-awards-to-citys-top-contributors-1899784)[Karnataka Guv Presents 'Namma Bengaluru Awards' To City's Top Contributors](https://www.deccanchronicle.com/southern-states/karnataka/karnataka-guv-presents-namma-bengaluru-awards-to-citys-top-contributors-1899784)

Participants reported feeling lighter and more flexible while performing asanas in water, attributing it to reduced pressure on the muscles. They also noted that the buoyancy made it easier to maintain poses for longer durations.

The event, blending physical discipline with creativity and environmental awareness, offered a fresh perspective on yoga and its adaptability. Organisers said the event is aimed at promoting a healthy lifestyle and demonstrating India's evolving innovations in wellness practices.

# CM Siddaramaiah to inaugurate 'State Olympics 2025' on January 17 in Mangaluru

Deputy Commissioner Mullai Muhilan M P said that the State Olympics meet organised by the Karnataka Olympic Association will be held in Mangaluru and Udupi from January 17 to 23.

[Naina J A](https://www.deccanherald.com/author/naina-j-a)

DHNS

Last Updated : 30 December 2024, 05:39 IST

Follow Us :

Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah.

Mangaluru: [Karnataka](https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka) Chief Minister [Siddaramaiah](https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/siddaramaiah) will inaugurate 'State Olympics 2025', at Mangala Stadium in [Mangaluru](https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/mangaluru) on January 17.

Addas your preferred

The State Olympics meet organised by the Karnataka Olympic Association will be held in Mangaluru and Udupi from January 17 to 23, said Deputy Commissioner Mullai Muhilan M P.

The last edition of the State Olympics was held at Dharwad. Around 1,800 athletes are likely to take part in the events in Mangaluru.

The district administration is arranging accommodation for around 2,500 people including athletes, delegates and others in Mangaluru, he told media people.

ADVERTISEMENT

The DC said that the events which will be held in Mangaluru are basketball, fencing (US Mally indoor stadium), football (Nehru Maidan), handball (Mangala stadium), kho-kho (Neru Maidan), netball (Mangala Stadium), swimming (Emmekere international swimming pool), taekwondo, wushu (Karnataka State Government Employees Hall, Hampankatte), volleyball (Mangala stadium), weight lifting (Ambedkar Bhavana), badminton (Marena indoor stadium, KMC Attavar).

# Karnataka Is Hosting India Paddle Festival 2025; From Date To Events, All You Need To Know

## The India Paddle Festival 2025, India's sole international Stand-Up Paddle (SUP) event, was inaugurated by Priyank Kharge

by [Jyotismita Maitra](https://curlytales.com/author/jyotismita/ "Author") Updated: February 24, 2025 5:24 PM

Share

[facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fcurlytales.com%2Fkarnataka-is-hosting-india-paddle-festival-2025-from-date-to-events-all-you-need-to-know%2F&utm_src=soc_fb "facebook")[twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Check+out+this+article:%20Karnataka+Is+Hosting+India+Paddle+Festival+2025%3B+From+Date+To+Events%2C+All+You+Need+To+Know%20-%20https%3A%2F%2Fcurlytales.com%2Fkarnataka-is-hosting-india-paddle-festival-2025-from-date-to-events-all-you-need-to-know%2F&utm_src=soc_tw "twitter")[whatsapp](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=Karnataka+Is+Hosting+India+Paddle+Festival+2025%3B+From+Date+To+Events%2C+All+You+Need+To+Know%20%0A%0A%20https%3A%2F%2Fcurlytales.com%2Fkarnataka-is-hosting-india-paddle-festival-2025-from-date-to-events-all-you-need-to-know%2F&utm_src=soc_wa "whatsapp")[pinterest](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcurlytales.com%2Fkarnataka-is-hosting-india-paddle-festival-2025-from-date-to-events-all-you-need-to-know%2F&utm_src=soc_pi&description=Karnataka+Is+Hosting+India+Paddle+Festival+2025%3B+From+Date+To+Events%2C+All+You+Need+To+Know "pinterest")[email](mailto:?subject=Karnataka+Is+Hosting+India+Paddle+Festival+2025%3B+From+Date+To+Events%2C+All+You+Need+To+Know&BODY=https%3A%2F%2Fcurlytales.com%2Fkarnataka-is-hosting-india-paddle-festival-2025-from-date-to-events-all-you-need-to-know%2F&utm_src=soc_mail "email")

[Join us](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029Va2AuC16WaKeKr37YT2a "Join us")[Follow us](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAqBwgKMMfZxgsw6vTdAw?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen "Follow us")

The India Paddle Festival 2025, India’s sole international Stand-Up Paddle (SUP) event, was inaugurated by Priyank Kharge, Minister of Rural Development & Panchayat Raj, IT & BT, at a function at Sahyadri Campus on Saturday.

Hosted by Incredible India and Karnataka Tourism, the festival released its official creatives alongside a promotional video of its inaugural success.Scheduled from March 7 to 9 at Sasihithlu Beach, the India Paddle Festival 2025 aims to position stand-up paddleboarding and surfing tourism while carving Karnataka’s shoreline into a leading destination in water sports globally.

## **India Paddle Festival 2025: Encouraging Adventure Tourism In Karnataka**

> View this post on Instagram
>
> [A post shared by Surfing Swami Foundation (@surfingswamifoundation)](https://www.instagram.com/p/DGYDnefSXoG/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

Addressing the launch, Minister Priyank Kharge underlined the festival’s contribution towards developing adventure tourism in Karnataka. ‘Karnataka’s beautiful coastline is the ideal backdrop for international competitions such as this.

The state’s rapid development of coastal sports, particularly surfing and stand-up paddleboarding, is quite impressive. We continue to support efforts that promote adventure tourism and local sports,’ he stated.

The event is being hosted by the Surfing Swami Foundation and will include top international paddlers from the Association of Paddle Surf Professionals World Tour, along with up-and-coming Indian players competing on an international level.

**Also Read: [Karnataka Is Hosting Its 1st Book And Cultural Festival At Bengaluru’s Vidhana Soudha; From Date To Events, All You Need To Know](https://curlytales.com/karnataka-is-hosting-its-1st-book-and-cultural-festival-at-bengalurus-vidhana-soudha-from-date-to-events-all-you-need-to-know/)**

## Creating A Thriving Water Sports Culture In India

> View this post on Instagram
>
> [A post shared by India Paddle Festival (@indiapaddlefestival)](https://www.instagram.com/p/DGYCbsTzht_/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

Ram Mohan Paranjape, head of the Surfing Swami Foundation, highlighted the India Paddle Festival 2025 as a platform for sustainable growth and the development of water sports in India. “With top-level competitions, mass events, and workshops, the festival will fill an action-packed calendar and place India on the map for SUP,” he further added.

Through the fusion of competitive and community events, the India Paddle Festival 2025 is likely to attract major international players, adventure sports enthusiasts, and tourist attention, further cementing India’s status as a leading player in the sport of stand-up paddleboarding.

Whether you are a sportsperson, a water sports athlete, or a simple person seeking an experience unlike any other near the sea, there is something for everyone in this festival.

**Also Read:** [Delhi Tulip Festival 2025: From 1 Lakh Tulips For Sale To Cultural Events, All You Need To Know About This Floral Extravaganza](https://curlytales.com/delhi-tulip-festival-2025-from-1-lakh-tulips-for-sale-to-cultural-events-all-you-need-to-know-about-this-floral-extravaganza/#google_vignette)

**Where:** Sasihithlu Beach, Mangalore, Karnataka.

**When**: 7th to 9th March, 2025

**Entry Fee:** ₹5,000 for Indian Athletes & ₹6,500 for Foreign Athletes

The question now is — will you be surfing the waves or watching from the shore?

# Mangaluru 'dasara' to begin on October 3; cultural events, marathon to mark grand celebrations

The grand 'dasara' procession will be held on October 13 with the procession of idols of Mahaganapathi, Navadurge, Sharada and colourful tableaus and art teams.

[Naina J A](https://www.deccanherald.com/author/naina-j-a)

DHNS

Last Updated : 30 September 2024, 05:12 IST

Follow Us :

0

File photo of dasara celebrations in Mangalru's Kudroli Sri Gokarnanatha Temple in Mangaluru as the idol of Goddess Sharada is carried towards 'Shobhayatre' procession.

Credit: DH File Photo

Mangaluru: The Mangaluru Dasara mahotsava will be held at the Kudroli Sri Gokarnanatha Temple from October 3 to 14, temple president H S Sairam has said. The 'dasara' will be flagged off by veteran leader Janardhan Poojary with the installation idol of Sharada and 'navadurga'.

Thousands of devotees are expected to take part in the dasara and Navarathri celebrations. The temple has made all the arrangements for celebrations, Sairam told mediapersons on Monday.

The Dasara Mahotsav will begin with the guru puja celebrations followed by various rituals.

Treasurer Padmaraj R said that rituals like _Durga homa_ (Oct 4), _Panchadurga homa_ (Oct 5), _Arya Durga homa_ (Oct 6), _Ambika Durga Homa_ (Oct 7), _Bhagavathi Durga homa_ (Oct 8), _Chandika homa_ (Oct 9), _Mahishamardini Durga homa_ (Oct 10), _Chandika homa hagalotsava_ (Oct 11), _Saraswati Durga homa_ (Oct 12), _Vageshwari Durga homa_ (Oct 13) will be held.

ADVERTISEMENT

The grand 'dasara' procession will be held on October 13 with the procession of idols of Mahaganapathi, Navadurge, Sharada and colourful tableaus and art teams. The idols will be immersed in the temple lake in the wee hours of October 14. Kerala chende, folk teams, dance troupes, dola dance by Maharashtrian artistes, Kalladka Gombe, colourful umbrellas from Thrissur, tiger dance, tableaux of various temples will add colours to the procession, he said.

**Auction of stalls**

To a query on auction of stalls by the Mangaluru City Corporation, Padmaraj said, “The High Court has directed the MCC to follow the due procedure while auctioning stalls during temple fairs. Accordingly, the MCC has decided to auction the stalls. However, the temple committee has urged the Deputy Commissioner and MCC Commissioner not to allot stalls inside the arch leading to the temple and in temple premises. Allowing the traders to set up stalls inside the arch will cause inconvenience to the devotees especially senior citizens visiting the temple.”

**Half marathon**

As a part of 'dasara' celebrations, a half marathon covering 21-km will be organised on October 6 at 5.30 am. About 1,500 to 2,000 people are likely to take part in the half marathon. Last year, a walkathon was organised, said Padmaraj.

Cultural programmes will be held daily from 6 pm at the temple premises, he added.

To a query on grandeur of Mangaluru Dasara, Janardhan Poojary said “All the credit of 'dasara' grandeur goes to the god. It's people’s 'dasara'.

[Mangaluru](https://www.aninews.in/topic/mangaluru) ( [Karnataka](https://www.aninews.in/topic/karnataka)) \[India\], December 6 (ANI): Locals on Sunday celebrated ' [Kesard Onji Dina](https://www.aninews.in/topic/kesard-onji-dina)' (a day in slushy water) with great pomp and show in [Karnataka](https://www.aninews.in/topic/karnataka)'s [Mangaluru](https://www.aninews.in/topic/mangaluru).

Children and women participated in ' [Kesard Onji Dina](https://www.aninews.in/topic/kesard-onji-dina)' which has been organized by Vijaya Yuva Sangama at Yekkur on the outskirts of [Mangaluru](https://www.aninews.in/topic/mangaluru).According to the programme organiser, the purpose of this event is to create awareness about agriculture and sports associated with it.The event included a running race, reverse running race, Kabaddi, volleyball, throw ball etc. (ANI)

# Mangaluru Dasara Event From September 26, 10 lakh People Expected To Attend

## More than 10 lakh people from various districts are expected to arrive in the city for the celebrations and preparations are on to hold the festival on a grand scale, said B Janaradhan Poojary.

Read Time: 2 mins
